mainTopic: Which offerings stay on the מזבח and which come down: early-placed אימורים, blemishes and נרבע, עולא on fire taking hold, and attached bones and hooves
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: disqualified innards are still rinsed, even with some risk of a mistake, so that holy offerings do not lie around like a carcass. Next, רבי יוחנן asks about אימורי קדשים קלים that went up on the מזבח before זריקת הדם. In two versions of the story the question is either about ירידה or about מעילה, and both end with the same ruling: לא ירדו, ואין בהן מעילה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. רבי יוחנן limits רבי עקיבא's leniency to small eye blemishes on an animal that was consecrated before it got the blemish, so a female עולה comes down even for רבי עקיבא. רבי ירמיה asks whether נרבע disqualifies birds, and רבה and רב נחמן בר יצחק prove that it does. The גמרא explains what רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים adds, and עולא rules that once the fire has taken hold of an offering, it goes up. A new משנה lists items that come down even if they went up. It also teaches that bones, horns and hooves go up only while they are still attached. A ברייתא gives the פסוקים behind that rule, and the גמרא begins to explain why both פסוקים are needed, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why help the כהנים toward a mistake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the practice of rinsing disqualified innards, since clean-looking innards might lead a כהן to offer them by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we really do something for the כהנים that could make them stumble?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea of rinsing disqualified innards. Rinsing them could cause a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dirty innards would never be put on the מזבח. Once they are washed, they look like proper innards, and a כהן might offer them by mistake. So why wash them at all?

keyTerms.meaning: A stumbling block, something that leads to a mistake
Shall we stand and do? (a sharp, rhetorical way of asking)

phrases.english: And shall we stand and do for the priests
something through which they will come to a stumbling block?!
phrases.notes: The worry is that once the innards are clean, a כהן could mix them up with good ones and put them on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling from the previous section (on 85a) that disqualified innards are rinsed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of rinsing disqualified innards
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rinsing makes disqualified innards look valid, so it creates a risk that a כהן will offer them by mistake.

steps.title: Respect for holy things comes first
steps.stepSummary: Even with the risk, rinsing is better, so that holy offerings do not lie around like a disgusting carcass.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, it is better this way, so that holy offerings will not be left lying around like a carcass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Rinsing is still the better choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits there is some risk of a mistake. But leaving קדשי שמים dirty and messy would be a disgrace. That concern for respect outweighs the risk.

keyTerms.meaning: It is preferable, better
Holy offerings that belong to Heaven
An animal carcass, something disgraceful

phrases.english: Even so, it is preferable,
so that the holy offerings of Heaven
will not be lying around like a carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing priorities: respect for holy things outweighs the risk
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The risk of a mistake should stop us from rinsing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rinsing is still better, because קדשי שמים must not be treated like a carcass.
steps.whatToRemember: Disqualified innards are still rinsed, out of respect for holy things, even though this carries a small risk of a mistake.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's question: must they come down?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks: if the אימורים of קדשים קלים were put on the מזבח before the blood was sprinkled, must they be taken down?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן asked: the fat parts of lower-level offerings were put on the מזבח before their blood was sprinkled. Must they come down, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן raises a question (בעיא) about offerings that were put on the מזבח too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קדשים קלים, the sprinkling of the blood (זריקה) is what makes the אימורים ready for the מזבח. Here they went up before that happened. The question is whether being on the מזבח is enough that they stay there.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raises an unresolved question
The fat parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Offerings of lower holiness, like a שלמים
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
They shall come down (from the מזבח)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said,
Rabbi Yochanan asks:
The sacrificial fats of offerings of lesser holiness
that someone brought up before their blood was sprinkled,
shall they come down or shall they not come down?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question that relates to the topic of things brought up onto the מזבח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must אימורי קדשים קלים that went up before זריקה be taken down?

steps.title: רבי אמי: ask about מעילה instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי tells רבי יוחנן that the better question is whether these אימורים are subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: You should be asking about מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי pushes back on the question itself. He suggests that a different question would be more fitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי thinks the real doubt is about מעילה, the prohibition of using holy property. It is the מעילה question, not the ירידה question, that seems unclear to him.

keyTerms.meaning: You should be asking (about something else)
The prohibition of using holy property for personal benefit

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
You should be asking about מעילה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which question רבי יוחנן chose to ask in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The focus of רבי יוחנן's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubt seems to be about מעילה, so asking about ירידה looks like the wrong question.

steps.title: Only זריקה decides מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that מעילה is clear, because only זריקה brings these parts under מעילה. His real doubt is about ירידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am not asking about מעילה. It is the sprinkling that puts them under מעילה. What I am asking about is whether they come down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his question. He explains why מעילה is not in doubt for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קדשים קלים, only the זריקה brings the אימורים under מעילה. Going up on the מזבח does not do this. So with no זריקה, there is clearly no מעילה. The only open question is whether they stay on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: I am asking, I have a doubt
Establishes, fixes the status
Coming down from the מזבח

phrases.english: He said to him:
About מעילה I have no question,
since it is the sprinkling that fixes them in מעילה;
what he was asking about is coming down.
phrases.notes: The wording suddenly says "he" instead of "I", but it is still רבי יוחנן's own question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the suggested question is already settled
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going up on the מזבח might bring the parts under מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only זריקה brings them under מעילה, so the real doubt is about ירידה.

steps.title: Resolution: they stay up, with no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers his own question: the parts do not come down, and there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He resolved it: they do not come down, and there is no מעילה on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers his own question and gives the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the parts are on the מזבח, they stay there, even though the זריקה has not happened yet. Still, they are not subject to מעילה, because only זריקה does that.

keyTerms.meaning: He resolved (the question)

phrases.english: And he resolved it:
they do not come down, and they are not subject to מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפָשֵׁיט: לֹא יֵרְדוּ, וְאֵין בָּהֶן מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אימורי קדשים קלים put on the מזבח before זריקה stay there, but they are not subject to מעילה.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רבי יוחנן's doubt was about ירידה, and he ruled: לא ירדו, ואין בהן מעילה.

steps.title: Second version: the question is about מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches it differently: רבי יוחנן's question was whether these early-placed אימורים are subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches it this way: רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן asked: the fat parts of lower-level offerings were put on the מזבח before their blood was sprinkled. Are they subject to מעילה or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same story. In this version, רבי יוחנן's question is about מעילה instead of ירידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is exactly the same as before. Only the topic of the question changes. Here, being placed on the מזבח might be what brings the parts under מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (a different version)

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak teaches it this way:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said,
Rabbi Yochanan asks:
The sacrificial fats of offerings of lesser holiness
that someone brought up before their blood was sprinkled,
are they subject to מעילה or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the case from step 3, but with a different question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does going up on the מזבח before זריקה bring the parts under מעילה?
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case. It is the same story told a second way, with the two questions swapped.

steps.title: רבי אמי: ask about ירידה instead
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי אמי suggests the better question is whether the parts come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: You should be asking about coming down!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי pushes back again, but this time he points to ירידה as the question to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 4. רבי אמי thinks ירידה is the unclear issue.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
You should be asking about coming down!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the focus of the question in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The focus of רבי יוחנן's question in the second version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubt seems to be about ירידה, so asking about מעילה looks like the wrong question.

steps.title: They became the מזבח's bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says ירידה is clear: once on the מזבח, the parts have become the מזבח's food. His real doubt is about מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am not asking about coming down, because they have become the bread of the מזבח. What I am asking about is מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that ירידה is obvious to him, so his real question is מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the parts go up, they count as the מזבח's food (לחמו של מזבח), so they clearly stay there. The open question is whether that also brings them under מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The "bread" (food) of the מזבח: what belongs to the מזבח to be burned

phrases.english: He said to him:
About coming down I have no question,
since they have become the bread of the altar;
what I am asking about is מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the suggested question is already settled
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Parts that went up too early might have to come down.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once on the מזבח, they are its food and stay there, so the real doubt is מעילה.

steps.title: Same resolution in both versions
steps.stepSummary: Here too, רבי יוחנן rules that the parts do not come down and are not subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He resolved it this way: they do not come down, and there is no מעילה on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version ends with the same ruling as the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions disagree only about which part was in doubt for רבי יוחנן. The final law is the same: the parts stay on the מזבח, and there is no מעילה.

phrases.english: And he resolved it this way:
they do not come down, and they are not subject to מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפָשֵׁיט הָכִי: לֹא יֵרְדוּ, וְאֵין בָּהֶן מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both versions agree: אימורי קדשים קלים placed on the מזבח before זריקה stay up, but they are not subject to מעילה.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions only swap which issue was in doubt. The bottom line is the same: לא ירדו, ואין בהן מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two separate ideas. Being on the מזבח decides whether the parts stay up. Only זריקה brings קדשים קלים under מעילה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about offerings disqualified outside the קודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of offerings whose disqualification did not start in the קודש, which includes blemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And these are the ones whose disqualification was not [in the קודש], etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to open a new discussion. This is setup: the next step, רבי יוחנן's comment, explains part of this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that animals disqualified before they ever entered the קודש, like a רובע, a נרבע or a בעל מום, must come down even if they were put on the מזבח. רבי עקיבא disagrees about blemished animals and says they stay up. רבי יוחנן will now define how far רבי עקיבא's leniency goes.

keyTerms.meaning: their disqualification
a blemished animal
'etc.', meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: And these are the ones whose disqualification was not, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה ends 'in the קודש'. It means animals that were already unfit before they ever got to the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יוחנן's question about early-placed אימורים and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings disqualified before entering the קודש come down from the מזבח. רבי עקיבא holds that blemished ones do not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits רבי עקיבא to small eye blemishes consecrated first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי עקיבא's leniency covers only small blemishes on the eye, which do not disqualify birds, and only when the animal was consecrated before it got the blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי עקיבא only allowed animals with small blemishes on the eye, since such blemishes are fine for bird offerings. And that is only when the animal was consecrated before it got the blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי עקיבא's leniency is much narrower than it first looks. It applies only to certain small blemishes, and only in a certain order of events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small eye blemishes do not disqualify a bird offering, so such a blemish is not a total disqualification for the מזבח. That is why רבי עקיבא lets the animal stay up once it is there. The second condition matters too: if the animal was consecrated while still unblemished, it was once fit for the מזבח. If it already had the blemish when consecrated, it was never fit.

keyTerms.meaning: deemed fit, here meaning it does not come down
small blemishes on the cornea of the eye
birds, bird offerings
consecration of the animal
blemish

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not say blemished animals may be brought on the מזבח in the first place. He only says that a small-blemished animal already placed on the מזבח does not come down.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rabbi Akiva deemed fit only
small blemishes on the cornea of the eye,
since they are fit in birds.
phrases.notes: A bird with this kind of small blemish may still be brought as an offering.

phrases.english: And that is when their consecration came before their blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֶלָּא בְּדוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's leniency applies only to small eye blemishes, and only when consecration came before the blemish.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees a female עולה comes down
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that רבי עקיבא agrees a female animal brought as an עולה comes down, since it counts like a blemish that came before consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא agrees about a female עולה, because it is like a case where the blemish came before the consecration.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds one more case where even רבי עקיבא says the offering comes down: a female animal brought as an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be male, so a female was never fit to be an עולה from the moment it was consecrated. Its 'problem' existed before the consecration. That matches the condition from the previous step, so רבי עקיבא's leniency does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees, concedes
a female animal brought as an עולה
it is like, it is comparable

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי עקיבא lets a blemished offering stay on the מזבח only when the blemish is small enough to be acceptable in birds and the animal was fit when consecrated. A female עולה was never fit, so it comes down.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva concedes regarding a female burnt offering,
that it is like a case where its blemish came before its consecration.
phrases.notes: Being female counts as its 'blemish' for an עולה, and it was female from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'consecration before blemish' condition from step 12 to a female עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female עולה comes down from the מזבח even according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks whether a bird can be disqualified as נרבע
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the disqualification of an animal used in bestiality (נרבע) applies to birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: Is there a נרבע disqualification for birds, or is there no נרבע disqualification for birds?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה opens a new question: if a person sinned with a bird, is that bird disqualified as an offering the way a נרבע animal is?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists both רובע (an animal that was the active partner with a person) and נרבע (an animal that was the passive object). A bird cannot be a רובע. The question is whether it can still be a נרבע.

keyTerms.meaning: asked, raised a question that he could not settle
an animal that was the object of bestiality
an animal that was the active partner in bestiality with a person

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
Is there a nirba disqualification for birds,
or is there no nirba disqualification for birds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from blemishes to another disqualification in the משנה's list, נרבע, and asks about birds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a bird used in bestiality is disqualified as a נרבע.

steps.title: First side: נרבע is tied to רובע, so birds are excluded
steps.stepSummary: One possibility: the פסוק 'מן הבהמה' excludes רובע and נרבע together, so wherever רובע does not apply, נרבע does not apply either, and birds are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the פסוק say 'of the animals' to exclude both the רובע and the נרבע together? Then wherever there is a רובע disqualification there is a נרבע one, and wherever there is no רובע disqualification there is no נרבע one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the first side of רבי ירמיה's question: perhaps נרבע always goes together with רובע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both disqualifications come from the same פסוק, so maybe they are a pair. A bird cannot be a רובע, so by this logic it also cannot be disqualified as a נרבע.

keyTerms.meaning: 'of the animals', from the פסוק about bringing offerings
to exclude
it applies / it does not apply

phrases.english: Did it say: “of the animals” –
to exclude the animal that copulated and the one that was copulated with;
so anywhere it applies to the active animal
it applies to the passive animal,
and anywhere it does not apply to the active animal
it does not apply to the passive animal;
phrases.notes: A bird can't be the active one, so on this side a bird can't be a נרבע either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the shared פסוק links נרבע to רובע so that the two always go together.

steps.title: Second side: a sin was done with it
steps.stepSummary: The other possibility: the bird is disqualified anyway, because a sin was committed with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is disqualified anyway, since a sin was committed with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question: maybe what disqualifies a נרבע is simply that a sin was done with it, and that is true of a bird too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this side, נרבע is not tied to רובע. The reason for the disqualification is the sin itself, so a bird used in bestiality would be disqualified. The next step, רבה's proof, answers the question.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps, which introduces the second side of a question
a sin was committed with it

steps.whyThisMatters: The question hinges on the reason behind נרבע: is it a technical pairing from the פסוק with רובע, or is it about the sin done with the animal?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, הֲרֵי נֶעֶבְדָה בּוֹ עֲבֵירָה?
phrases.english: Or perhaps, a sin was nevertheless committed with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, הֲרֵי נֶעֶבְדָה בּוֹ עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite side of the question from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the sin done with the bird is enough on its own to disqualify it, regardless of רובע.

steps.title: רבה proves from רבי עקיבא that נרבע disqualifies birds
steps.stepSummary: רבה points out that רבי עקיבא lets blemished animals stay on the altar once they went up only because the same blemish is fine for birds. If נרבע were fine for birds, רבי עקיבא should allow a נרבע animal for the same reason. He does not, so נרבע must disqualify birds too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Come and hear. רבי עקיבא allows blemished animals to stay on the altar. If a נרבע bird were fit, he should also allow a נרבע animal, since it would be fit among birds. Learn from this that a נרבע bird is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers רבי ירמיה's question with a proof. He shows that נרבע does disqualify a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's reason is: whatever is fit for birds should not be sent down from the altar when it shows up in an animal. If a נרבע bird were fit, that same reason would protect a נרבע animal. Since רבי עקיבא does not protect a נרבע animal, a נרבע bird must be unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds it valid
Blemished animals
Since
Learn from this: the conclusion of a proof

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not hold that a נרבע animal is valid. רבה uses the fact that he does NOT say so as his proof.

phrases.english: Rabba said: Come and hear:
Rabbi Akiva deems blemished animals valid.
phrases.notes: This means the small eye blemishes from the earlier steps, which do not disqualify birds.

phrases.english: And if it is so (that a נרבע bird is fit),
let us also deem valid an animal that was the object of bestiality,
since it is valid among birds!
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from steps 14-16
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's reasoning in the משנה, which validates blemishes that are fit for birds

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings support from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists a נרבע bird with other unfit birds and says they all make a person's clothes impure when he swallows them. This shows that the מליקה did not make them proper offerings, so they are unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this in a ברייתא: a bird that was נרבע, מוקצה, worshipped, אתנן, מחיר, a טומטום, or an אנדרוגינוס, all of these make clothes impure when they are in the throat. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a second support, from a ברייתא, that a נרבע bird is unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a valid bird offering is killed by מליקה, the מליקה counts as proper killing, so the bird is not a נבלה. These birds still make clothes impure the way a bird נבלה does. That means the מליקה did not work for them, because they are unfit offerings. A נרבע bird is on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this in a teaching: brings support
Set aside for idol worship
Payment given to a זונה
Something received in trade for a dog
The throat, at the moment of swallowing

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer to רבי ירמיה: the disqualification of נרבע applies to birds as well.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
We too learned it:
A bird that was the object of bestiality, or set aside for idolatry, or worshipped,
or given as a harlot's payment, or as the price of a dog,
or a tumtum, or a hermaphrodite,
all of them render garments impure when in the throat!
phrases.notes: That is the law of a bird נבלה, so the מליקה did not count for these birds.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof after רבה's
steps.raayaObject: A נרבע bird is unfit as an offering
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists a נרבע bird among birds whose מליקה leaves them as נבלה

steps.title: What does רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, who reported that his father would push blemished animals off the altar. It asks what he adds, since the first opinion in the משנה already said they come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, and so on. What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks why רבי חנינא's statement is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה already rules that blemished animals come down from the altar. רבי חנינא's report that his father pushed them off seems to add nothing new. The גמרא wants to know what he is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: Deputy כהן גדול
What is he teaching us? (it seems we already know this)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy High Priest, etc.
phrases.notes: He says his father would push blemished animals off the altar.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי חנינא adds beyond the first opinion in the משנה

steps.title: First answer: he reports a real event
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא is telling us about an event that actually happened. This shows the law was carried out in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: he is teaching us about an actual event.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: רבי חנינא adds a real event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself is not new. What is new is the report that a כהן actually acted on it. That shows the law was done in practice and was not only discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces one of several answers
An actual event

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
he teaches us an incident,

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעית אימא: מעשה קא משמע לן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The point is a real event that shows the law was done in practice

steps.title: Second answer: he removed them quietly
steps.stepSummary: The word דוחה teaches how the animals were removed: quietly, in a back-handed way, not in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: what does 'push off' mean? In a back-handed way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רבי חנינא's new point is the way the animals were taken down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, רבי חנינא adds a detail about how it was done. His father removed the blemished animals quietly, in an unusual back-handed way, and not openly.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushes off
In a back-handed, unusual way

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new law about whether the animals come down. Everyone agrees they come down. This answer is only about how they are taken down.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What is 'would reject'? In a backhanded manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He teaches that the animals were removed quietly, in a back-handed way

steps.title: עולא limits 'if it came down, it does not go back up'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a disqualified offering that came down does not go back up. עולא says this is only true if the fire has not yet taken hold of it. If the fire has taken hold, it goes back up.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Just as if it went up, and so on. עולא said: They taught this only when the fire has not taken hold of them. But if the fire has taken hold of them, they go back up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה, and עולא limits when it applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is: just as a disqualified offering that went up does not come down, one that came down does not go back up. עולא says this applies only before the fire has taken hold. Once the fire has taken hold of it, it goes back up even if it came down.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only: introduces a limit on a rule
The fire has taken hold of them
They go back up

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that once the altar's fire has taken hold, the offering is treated as belonging to the altar.

phrases.english: Just as if it ascended, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: so too, if it came down, it does not go back up.

phrases.english: Ulla said: They taught this only
where the fire has not taken hold of them,
but if the fire has taken hold of them, they shall ascend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'If it came down, it does not go back up' applies only before the fire takes hold. After that, it goes back up.

steps.title: Two versions of where עולא's rule applies
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says עולא's rule about fire was said on our משנה. רב חנינא מסורא says it was said on the next משנה, about bones, tendons, horns and hooves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי teaches עולא's statement on the first clause. רב חנינא of Sura teaches it on the later clause: 'The bones, the tendons, the horns and the hooves: when they are attached, they go up; if they came apart, they do not go up.' עולא said: They only taught this when the fire has not yet taken hold of them. But if the fire has taken hold of them, they go up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of עולא's rule from step 22. In this version, the rule is attached to a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב מרי's version, עולא is talking about disqualified offerings that came down from the altar. In רב חנינא's version, עולא is talking about bones, tendons, horns and hooves that came apart from the animal. Either way the rule is the same: once the fire has taken hold, the item goes back up.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches, meaning he places a statement on a certain part of the text
the first part or clause
the later part or clause
still attached to the animal
they came apart from the animal
the fire has taken hold of them

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not saying two different things. The words of his rule stay the same. The argument is only about which משנה he was talking about.

phrases.english: Rav Mari teaches it on the first clause;
phrases.notes: 'It' means עולא's rule from step 22. The 'first clause' is our משנה about disqualified offerings.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina of Sura teaches it on the later clause:
phrases.notes: The 'later clause' is the next משנה, which the גמרא quotes right now.

phrases.english: The bones and the tendons
and the horns and the hooves,
when they are attached, they go up,
if they came apart, they do not go up.
Ulla said:
They only taught this
when the fire has not taken hold of them,
but if the fire has taken hold of them, they go up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי מַתְנֵי אַרֵישָׁא; רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא מַתְנֵי אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of where עולא's rule from step 22 applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bones, tendons, horns and hooves that came apart do not go up. עולא says this is only true before the fire takes hold of them; after that, they go up.

steps.title: How far each version reaches
steps.stepSummary: If עולא was talking about the later clause, his rule surely applies to the first clause too. If he was talking about the first clause, it does not apply to bones and hooves, because they are not meant to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who teaches it on the later clause, all the more so it applies to the first clause. And according to the one who teaches it on the first clause, it does not apply to the later clause, because those items are not fit for burning at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical difference between the two versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bones and hooves are not normally burned on the altar. So if fire can still make them go back up, it can surely make a real offering go back up, even a disqualified one. But if עולא only spoke about disqualified offerings, we cannot stretch his rule to bones and hooves, which were never meant to be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: all the more so
fit to be burned on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: The version on the later clause gives עולא's rule the widest reach. It covers both disqualified offerings and bones and hooves. The version on the first clause covers only disqualified offerings.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the later clause:
all the more so on the first clause;
and the one who teaches it on the first clause:
but on the later clause, it does not apply,
since they are not fit for burning at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי אַסֵּיפָא – כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far each of the two versions in step 23 reaches.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Placing עולא's rule on the later clause makes it apply to both cases. Placing it on the first clause limits it to disqualified offerings.

steps.title: New משנה: items that must come down even if they went up
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists items that are not meant for the altar at all. If they went up, they must come down: offering meat that people eat, the leftover עומר, the שתי הלחם, the לחם הפנים, the leftovers of מנחות, and the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these, if they went up, come down: the meat of the most-holy offerings, the meat of the lesser-holy offerings, the leftover of the עומר, the two loaves, the showbread, the leftovers of the meal offerings, and the incense.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists things that must be taken down if they were put on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the rule was that some unfit items stay up once they went up. These items are different: they were never meant to be burned on this altar at all. Most of them are meant to be eaten, so the altar does not hold on to them.

keyTerms.meaning: the most-holy offerings
the lesser-holy offerings
what is left of the עומר after the handful is burned
what is left of the meal offerings after the handful is burned
incense

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these, if they went up, come down:
the meat of the most-holy offerings,
and the meat of the lesser-holy offerings,
and the leftover of the omer,
and the two loaves, and the showbread,
and the leftovers of the meal offerings, and the incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves from items that stay up once they went up to items that must come down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items that were never meant to be burned on the altar must come down even if they went up.

steps.title: Wool, hair, bones and hooves: attached or separated
steps.stepSummary: Wool, hair, bones, tendons, horns and hooves go up when they are still attached to the animal, because the פסוק says to burn 'everything.' Once they came apart, they do not go up, because another פסוק mentions only the meat and the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wool on the heads of sheep, the hair in the beard of goats, the bones, the tendons, the horns and the hooves: when they are attached, they go up, as it says: 'And the priest shall burn it all.' If they came apart, they do not go up, as it says: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It explains when the hard parts of an animal are burned with it and when they are not, and gives a פסוק for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The priest shall burn it all' includes everything that is still part of the animal. 'The meat and the blood' limits the offering to the meat itself. So once these parts came apart, they are no longer included. This is the later clause that רב חנינא מסורא used in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: wool
goats
hooves
'and the priest shall burn it all'

steps.whatToRemember: Whether these parts go up depends on whether they are still attached. When attached, they go up because of 'הכל.' When separated, they do not go up because of 'הבשר והדם.' Remember that עולא, in רב חנינא's version, adds that once the fire has taken hold of them, they go up anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact text that רב חנינא מסורא used for עולא's rule. Seeing it in full makes the argument in steps 23 and 24 clear.

phrases.english: The wool on the heads of sheep,
and the hair in the beard of goats,
and the bones and the tendons
and the horns and the hooves;
when they are attached, they go up,
as it says: "And the priest shall burn it all."
If they came apart, they do not go up,
as it says: "And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new משנה with the case of an animal's hard parts, whether attached or separated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal's hard parts are burned while they are attached, based on 'הכל.' Once they came apart, they are not burned, based on 'הבשר והדם.'

steps.title: The word 'everything' includes bones, tendons, horns and hooves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word הַכֹּל ('everything') in ויקרא that bones, tendons, horns and hooves are burned on the מזבח along with the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: The רבנן taught: 'And the כהן shall burn everything on the מזבח.' This comes to include the bones, the tendons, the horns and the hooves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by giving the source for the משנה's rule. A ברייתא shows that the word 'everything' in the פסוק includes the hard, inedible parts of the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you might think only the meat of a קרבן goes on the מזבח. The extra word הַכֹּל teaches that bones, tendons, horns and hooves are also part of what is burned. This is the source for the first half of the משנה's rule in step 26.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall burn (on the מזבח)
Everything. This extra word teaches that more items are included.
To include (to add something extra)
Hooves

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
"And the priest shall burn everything on the altar"
to include the bones and the tendons
and the horns and the hooves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule that attached bones and hooves go up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word הַכֹּל includes bones, tendons, horns and hooves as items burned on the מזבח.

steps.title: Once they come apart, they are not burned
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether these parts are burned even after they come apart from the animal. It answers no, from the פסוק 'your עולות, the meat and the blood.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they go up even if they came apart from the animal. So the פסוק teaches: 'And you shall offer your עולות, the meat and the blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits the rule from step 27. It uses a second פסוק to show that bones and hooves that came apart from the animal do not go up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests a possible mistake: maybe הַכֹּל includes these parts even when they are separate. The פסוק in דברים mentions only 'the meat and the blood.' That teaches that only the meat, and things still attached to it, go up. This is the source for the second half of the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (a mistaken idea that is about to be corrected)
They came apart (from the animal)
The פסוק teaches (to correct the mistaken idea)
The meat and the blood

steps.whatToRemember: הַכֹּל includes attached bones, tendons, horns and hooves. 'The meat and the blood' leaves them out once they came apart.

phrases.english: One might think: even if they came apart?
The verse teaches:
"And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the inclusion from step 27 to parts that are still attached.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bones, tendons, horns and hooves that came apart from the animal are not burned on the מזבח.

steps.title: Starting a question about 'the meat and the blood'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to question the ברייתא's use of the words 'the meat and the blood.' The question continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learn from 'the meat and the blood,'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts to question how the ברייתא uses the פסוק 'the meat and the blood,' but the sentence finishes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words of the challenge appear here. The גמרא is about to examine what follows if we learn from this פסוק. The full point of the challenge will come in the next section.

phrases.english: If "the flesh and the blood,"

steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's learning from 'the meat and the blood' in step 28.
